title: Is this combat ruleset possible in RPG Maker ( MV ) or should i dedicate myself to learn other engines? (Dynamic Turns, Stamina System, D&D Style etc..)

posts.author: musty
posts.body:
Hey guys, i've never really looked into RPG Maker until i've played Fear and Hunger 1, i absolutely loved it and never tought this engine was capable of doing something like this
(i've always known about thousands of similar games with default assets and default gameplay and never got into them).
I'm also a very passionate D&D player and Dark Souls enjoyer so some years ago i've designed a
VERY AMATEUR
set of custom rules to run a One-Shot in Dark Souls D&D
(Which never actually ended up happening, i just did many test simulations to check that everything is balanced gameplay wise)
Recently after replaying Fear & Hunger and just now starting to play Funger2 Termina, i've tought about trying to develop something since this engine is pretty accessible, and i'm starting to learn drawing
(I will try my best to not copy-paste everything, i'll keep the ideas personal!!!).
So, i'm just gonna drop down a simplified version of my combat ruleset, how turns work etc... because i'm wondering if something like this is even possible since RPGMaker is also a lot restrictive:
I am sorry if this can get confusing, i've tried to make it as clear and simple as possible, i even cut out some more complex mechanics.
GAMEPLAY​
Stamina
Actions consume
Stamina
.
(Max stamina depends on: stats and equipment)
Stamina
is recovered at the start of each entity's turn.
(The amount recovered depends on: stats and equipment)
Using the
Support: Recover
or
Support: Interact
(with item)
actions restores additional stamina during the same turn
(Will go in-depth about actions soon)
.
If
Stamina
drops to 0:
Stamina is
not
automatically recovered on the next run.
The entity becomes
Exhausted
(status)
Stamina can only be restored using
Support Actions
Turns
At the start, each entity rolls
1d20 + Dexterity mod
. Turns are taken in descending order of the result.
During a turn:
The
attacker
may perform attacks
The
attacked
entity can
counterattack
with a Combat action
(again, will go in-depth soon)
If the
attacked
entity counterattacks, the
attacker
may choose to use a
Reaction Action
before rolling the attack dices.
(i know this can get confusing! sorry!)
An entity can defend outside their turn
ONLY
if they previously used Support Actions to
prepare defence
.
(again, in-depth very soon!)
Actions
Each turn, entities can perform the following types of actions:
Combat Actions
, Unlimited times
(limited by stamina)
Attack
: Stamina cost and damage vary by weapon
Heavy Attack
: Higher Stamina cost and damage, depending on the weapon.
Cast Spell
: Stamina cost and damage vary by spell
(No mana, limited use spells rechargable with items or resting)
Breakthroug
*: Destroys an active defense, fixed Stamina cost.
(Strenght Mod.)
Reaction Actions
, Once per counterattack received
during
their turn.
Dodge
: Completely avoid an attack
(Dexteryty Mod.)
Block
: Reduce damage taken with a shield
(Reduction based on shield roll + Resistance Mod.)
Parry
: Attempt to unbalace the attacker. If successfull, the next attack against them is
critical
. If failed, the defender becomes
unbalanced
(status)
Support Actions
, Once per turn.
Recover
: Restores additional Stamina (amount determined by entity class with a dice roll)
Interact
: Use an item from the inventory
Raise Shield
: Blocks the next attack received until the start of the next turn.
(Can be attempted to destroy by Combat Action Breakthrough)
Prepare Parry
: Allows a parry against the next attack received until the start of the next turn.
STATS
Strenght
: Affects strenght-based actions and attacks.
Dexterity
: Affects dexterity-based actions and attacks.
Intelligence
: Affects intellicence-based actions and attacks.
Resistance
: Determines maximum Stamina and Mod. for Block and Death Saving rolls.
Luck
: Affects luck-based actions
(Loot and narrative)
AC (Armor Class)
: Value that an attacker must exceed during an attack roll to hit.
I really hope this cleared up my vision and i really hope that this is something possible to do on RPG Maker MV, otherwise i'll dedicate my time learning other engines, Godot is what i was thinking about as an alternative.

To call Godot an alternative to RPG Maker is like calling a tomato an alternative to a hamburger.
If you need the gameplay systems that RPG Maker provides out of the box, then you're better of learning whatever you need to learn to modify RPG Maker to fully suit your vision. If you don't really need much of what RPG Maker provides, then yeah, go ahead and learn a more general-purpose tool.

I really don't think it's questionable at all. If you're using Godot, you start with
nothing
. It doesn't know what HP is. It doesn't know what damage is. It doesn't know that actors can attack enemies. If you're building all of that from scratch, I don't think there's any doubt that it would be harder than modding RPGMaker.
On the other hand, using Godot you don't have to start from scratch. There are probably a bunch of RPG frameworks that you could start from, and I have no idea whether modding one of those would be easier or harder than modding RPGMaker.
But in short, your professed advantage to Godot (that it gives you more freedom) isn't really real. You probably have just as much freedom in RPGMaker as you have in Godot, as long as you can manage source code modifications and/or plugins. And if you can't, then you
probably
shouldn't be using Godot.

I'm actually starting to figure some stuff out, managed to implement attack rolls with armor class on enemies with writing up custom plugins (obviously with the help of AI!)

posts.body:
Well, with ATK, DEF, MAT and MDF, you can basically do whatever you want, as long as your formula's use them right. But LUK and AGI are used for specific things in the battle engine. If you want want to use LUK and AGI for something completely different, note that you need plugins that nullifies the effect it now has in battle.
So putting LUK where AGI used to be, makes LUK act as if it is AGI. And Armor Class still act as LUK.

As JohnDoeGames said, you probably shouldn't switch Agility and Luck.
The first four parameters (Attack, Defence, M.Attack, and M.Defence) have absolutely no meaning to the engine – they do only what you tell them to do, usually by using them in damage formulas.
The same is not true for Agility and Luck.
In the base engine, agility affects turn order and the chance of being surprised or gaining the element of surprise against random encounters, while luck slightly adjusts the chances of being inflicted by a state and possibly a couple other things.
Thus, I'd recommend switching the order via a UI plugin, rather than by renaming them. Though there's also the alternative of finding or building a plugin that removes their default effects.
By the way, about AI, I definitely don't recommend using it, but as long as you think of it as a "dumb assistant" and treat anything it outputs with great caution, you might be able to get somewhere with it.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
It is absolutely doable and you can do pretty much all of what you want with just scripting and no special plugins. It all depends on how much effort you are willing to put in.
You could build a D&D-type game and manually create everything, making your own combat, classes, races, skills, spells, attributes, stats, inventory, enemies, menus, equipment, etc.
So, is it possible. Definitely yes.
It really just depends on how much of the default engine you want to use, how many pre-existing plugins you want to use, and how much you want to build from scratch with scripting.
The more you change and build manually, the more work it is going to be.
I have already done quite a few D&D-based experiments. If you are interested in what you can do that is a bit different, check out my YouTube channel where I recreated the Eye of the Beholder party creation process.
I also just made a demo video of a Yahtzee-Poker hybrid mechanic as part of a D&D-based project, just because it interests me.
There are also some developers making D&D-type games in RPG Maker now.
Anyway, good luck on your projects!

While what you want is probably possible. I must confess some of it is currently above my ability. Though you could possibly just rename either TP or MP stamina, make all actions cost it, bake in TP/MP regeneration into actors and enemies and develop from there.
What I don't know how to do is make actions unlimited and then end turn when you run out of stamina. But someone else probably have a solution.
As for dnd stats, most you can just rename the current attributes for. I once considered making luck into Charisma, but decided against it because I did not want to overcomplicate things. I actually like the default rpg maker mechanics.
Maybe you can do the following with attributes:
Strength=Physical Attack (Increases power of physical melee attacks)
Dexterity=Agility (Increases power of physical ranged attacks and determines turn order)
Constitution=Hp (Increases max HP and Physical Defenses)
Intelligence=Magic Attack (Increases MP and power of magical attacks for wizards)
Wisdom=Magic Defense (Increases magic defense and power of magical attacks for clerics)
Charisma=Luck (Decreases chance to be affected by ailments and power of magical attacks for sorcerers and warlocks. Unlocks dialogue options.)
